name: The Egerton House Hotel
positioning: Boutique townhouse hotel on a leafy residential street in Knightsbridge, a short walk from the Victoria and Albert Museum, with guest privileges at the V&A
best_for: Art and design lovers who want easy access to the V&A and Knightsbridge's museums
Travelers who prefer an intimate townhouse to a large hotel

facts.text: The hotel is in the heart of Knightsbridge, near Harrods, the Science Museum and the Victoria and Albert Museum.
The hotel sits on a tranquil, leafy residential street.
The hotel overlooks verdant, private residential gardens.
The Natural History Museum, the Royal Albert Hall and Kensington Palace and Gardens in Hyde Park are a short walk from the hotel.
The hotel occupies numbers 17 and 19 Egerton Terrace, which were already in use as a private hotel by the late 1890s.
The hotel displays original works of art by artists including Toulouse-Lautrec, Erte, Ludwig Bemelmans, Peanuts creator Charles M. Schulz, British cartoonist JAK and French caricaturist Sem.
Rooms have Savoir beds, luxury toiletries, and plush bathrobes and slippers.
Some Deluxe King rooms have full-height bay windows that catch the afternoon sunlight.
The studio suites have plush decor, refined artwork and bespoke amenities.
The hotel's V&A VIP cards give access to the V&A Members' Lounge and entry to all temporary exhibitions, including sold-out ones.
Traditional afternoon tea is served in the Tea Room, with loose-leaf tea and homemade treats.
Breakfast is served in the Dining Room or in your bedroom.

highlights.text: Through a long-standing partnership with the Victoria and Albert Museum, guests receive complimentary tickets to the V&A's feature exhibitions.
A limited number of V&A VIP access cards are available at reception each day.
The hotel's top suite, the V&A Suite, is named for its partnership with the Victoria and Albert Museum.
Guests' dogs can have a Pawtrait Experience with the hotel's resident artist, Shelly Levy.
The bar serves the hotel's signature martini.

considerations.text: The V&A VIP access cards are limited in number each day, so not every guest can have one on a given day.
Interleading rooms for four to five people depend on availability and must be booked directly through the hotel's reservations team.
WhataHotel notes compact room sizes typical of historic London properties.
